Every cue, and no cloth

Describe

Engine

Photograph, 3-D render or AI image? Say what in the picture decides — and what would not.

Critical

Volume and depth · Lecture C of 3

Alberti's window becomes a ratio

A 3-D program's virtual camera divides each point by its depth: twice as far, half as big. It is Alberti's construction, now computed millions of times a second.

Of all the projections employed in computer graphics, the perspective projection is one most widely used.

(Vince 2017, 204)

Image: Chart comparing graphical projections of the same house: multiview, axonometric, oblique and perspective.

Comparison of graphical projections · Cmglee (Wikimedia Commons user) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Source

  • Orthographic views (CLO pattern views) do not divide by depth; perspective does.

Alberti’s window, written as a ratio

  • Read the formula aloud once: divide by depth.

Volume and depth · Lecture C of 3

Painted order or tested depth?

A 2.5-D web layer is sorted back to front once. A 3-D engine stores a depth value for every pixel and tests it every frame, so crossing shapes stay honest.

Photogrammetry goes further and measures depth from many photos — but shiny, black or sheer cloth often scans badly.

Image: Diagram of a Z-buffer: a simple 3D scene and its depth image, where nearer surfaces are brighter.

Z buffer · -Zeus- (Wikimedia Commons user) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Source

  • 2.5-D parallax on a portfolio site is painter's order, not 3-D.
  • Marr's 2½-D sketch: depth per point, seen from one place.

Before you praise the depth, name the engine

Volume and depth · Lecture C of 3

Plausible is not the same as possible

Around 1750 Piranesi etched prisons whose stairs and bridges look convincing yet cannot all connect. Image generators make depth in a similar way: from learned plausibility, with no scene behind it.

Has the machine learned perspective, or only what perspective looks like?

Image: Piranesi’s etching The Drawbridge from the Imaginary Prisons: vast stairways and bridges that look convincing but cannot all connect.

Giovanni Battista Piranesi - Le Carceri d'Invenzione - First Edition - 1750 - 07 - The Drawbridge · Giovanni Battista Piranesi · Public domain · Source

  • Check an AI garment for: shadow direction, seam continuity, what holds the volume up.

Volume and depth · Lecture C of 3

AI gives images, not patterns

Fashion instructors interviewed in a 2026 study found AI tools useful for ideas but not for construction.

they just give you images; they don't actually support garment construction

(An and Park 2026, 15)

Fortuny's Delphos pleats are construction: no picture of them tells you how to make them.

Image: A pink pleated Delphos gown by Fortuny on a display figure; the fine pleats fall straight to the floor.

Pink Delphos dress by Fortuny, 1920s · Mabalu (photograph); Mariano Fortuny (dress) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Source

  • Same study, p. 14: instructors ask for process-oriented assessment, not output counts.

Volume and depth · Lecture C of 3

The tool explores; you judge

Margaret Boden separates exploring a style from transforming it. A tool can explore a learned space; judging what is valuable, and breaking the rule, stays with the designer.

This example illustrates the evaluation bottleneck that lies in the way of automated transformational creativity.

(Boden 2004, 320)

Image: Dresses by Rei Kawakubo in an exhibition view

Dresses by Rei Kawakubo - Sarah Stierch 02 · Sarah Stierch (photograph); Rei Kawakubo (garments) · CC BY 4.0 · Source

  • Boden's Lovelace questions (2004, 16): can computers help us understand creativity, or appear creative?

Who decides what counts as volume?

  • This loop is the Lab 2 protocol.

Volume and depth · Lecture C of 3

Whose pictures taught the machine?

Image generators learn from millions of pictures by people who were rarely asked. The ethicist Oliver Bendel notes outputs that still showed watermarks from image platforms.

it was repeatedly noticed that images bore watermarks and fonts

(Bendel 2025, 440)

This 1890 catalogue illustrator is public domain today. Who is paid when a living illustrator's style is learned?

Image: Página del catálogo de moda de Bloomingdale Bros., verano de 1890: grabados de cuatro trajes infantiles y un traje masculino a rayas, cada uno con su número de figura y de referencia.

Illustrated fashion catalogue - summer, 1890 (1890) (14781648884) · Bloomingdale Bros. · Internet Archive Book Images · Public domain · Source

Volume and depth · Lecture C of 3

Recall check

Alone, from memory, three minutes. Then compare with a partner.

  1. What does a virtual camera divide each point by?
  2. How does 2.5-D decide what is in front?
  3. What does a Z-buffer store for each pixel?
  4. Why is an AI image plausible but not proven?
  5. What did fashion instructors say AI cannot support?

Course geometric background · threshold · #c378606cc29b · Original course SVG

Answers:

  • Its depth (z).
  • By drawing order, back to front, once.
  • The nearest depth value, tested every frame.
  • It imitates cues from training images without a scene or camera.
  • Garment construction: they give images, not patterns.
